questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements :**

I. All A are T.

II. No T is N.

**Conclusions : **

I. Some N are T.

II. All N are A.

III. Some T are A.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e43a472ab6dfe83ea10e9c7791b61bc956c15dddd29bc4aafa152d2e981db1ca.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some N are T → Does not follow (As no T is N. So, as direct negative or cross relation between T and N is given, therefore it is definitely false)

II. All N are A → Does not follow (As all A are T and no T is N. So, as whole A comes in T which has direct negative or cross relation with N, therefore it is definitely false)

III. Some T are A → Follow (As all A are T. So, as whole A comes in T, therefore it is definitely true)

∴ Here, Only conclusion III follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "**Only conclusion III follows**"

→ 168 = 157 + 11

→ 326 ≠ 168 × 2 → Doesn't follow the logic.

**4) (117, 128, 266):**

→ 128 = 117 + 11

→ 266 ≠ 128 × 2 → Doesn't follow the logic.

Here, we can see that only option 1 follow the logic.

Hence, the correct answer is **"(169, 180, 360)"**.
